baselineNote: Every baseline below was computed from a live read-only pull of Romify's HubSpot on September 9, 2026, and reconciles to the figures published in the Signal Health Report and the HubSpot Read and Activation Plan.

entries.title: Lifecycle stamping is live
entries.why: Nothing downstream can be measured until this runs. MQL and SQL dates are blank on all 12,897 contacts, which is why Demand Health cannot be scored on conversion or velocity.
entries.metric: Contacts carrying an MQL or SQL date
entries.note: The workflow 26 | Set Marketing Stage on Contact Creation has been off since May 18, 2026. It only stamps contacts created after it is switched on, so every week it stays off is a week of measurement that cannot be recovered.

entries.title: The Demo done pile shrinks
entries.why: 48.3% of every deal Romify has ever lost was lost in this stage. Roughly 25 of the deals sitting here are live pilots whose Sales deal was never moved.
entries.metric: Open Sales deals held in Demo done, and their value
entries.target: 76 or fewer once live pilots are moved, then 60 or fewer
entries.note: Moving the live pilots is an hour of work and makes the number honest. Shrinking it further is the Evaluation stage plus a 30-day clock.

entries.title: Demo done to Pilot Negotiation conversion improves
entries.why: Every other step in the funnel converts between 70% and 96%. This one converts at 52.7% and it is the single largest source of lost revenue.
entries.metric: Share of deals entering Demo done that advance to Pilot Negotiation
entries.note: The new Evaluation stage splits this step in two. Report Demo done through to Pilot Negotiation as a combined measure so the trend line survives the change, and show Evaluation separately underneath.

entries.title: The renewal ladder actually moves
entries.why: 150 of 152 open renewals sit in the first bucket carrying $2,073,841. The stages are configured correctly. Nothing moves records through them.
entries.metric: Open renewals still sitting in the 12-months-out stage
entries.note: Ben confirmed on September 14 that nobody owns renewals today. Target state is sales pre-sale, Jonelle post-sale. One date-driven workflow does the mechanical part.

entries.title: Past-due close dates cleared
entries.why: 94 open deals worth $854,111 carry close dates that have already passed, which is 20% of open pipeline. The forecast the board sees is structurally stale.
entries.metric: Open deals whose close date is in the past
entries.note: Each one is either re-dated or closed lost. The record list makes this a working session rather than a hunt.

entries.title: Cold pipeline re-engaged
entries.why: 82 open Sales deals worth $865,825 show no logged activity in 60 days or more.
entries.metric: Open Sales deals with no logged HubSpot activity in 60 days or more
entries.note: MEASUREMENT CAVEAT. This counts logged HubSpot activity only. Megan is running wave-based re-engagement through a separate trial, personalised from the account owner, which does not write back to HubSpot. Until that activity is logged, this number overstates how much of the book is genuinely untouched. Closing that logging gap is itself part of the work.

entries.title: Industry backfilled where there is money on the table
entries.why: 1,934 companies have no industry set. 58 of them carry open pipeline worth $607,803, and vertical targeting is the exact capability Megan wants.
entries.metric: Companies with open pipeline and no industry set
entries.note: Fix the 58 with money attached first. The remaining 1,876 are dormant records and can be backfilled in bulk or left alone.

entries.title: Every contact has a reachable owner
entries.why: 1,879 contacts have nobody accountable: 1,121 with no owner set and 758 assigned to a deactivated user. The second group looks owned in HubSpot and is not, so nobody notices them.
entries.metric: Contacts with no owner, or an owner who has been deactivated
entries.note: Start with the deactivated-owner group. Those records are actively invisible rather than merely unassigned.

entries.title: Forecast probabilities corrected
entries.why: Pilot Done and Pending Feedback is set to 80% and the next stage, Pending Decision, is set to 40%, so a deal that moves forward halves its forecast value. Every renewal stage is set to 80% regardless of how close it is.
entries.note: Fifteen minutes of settings work. 14 deals sit in the first stage and 6 in the second. Actual renewal rate is 84% against a flat 80% across the whole ladder.

entries.title: Ian's win rate moves
entries.why: Ben asked for this directly on September 14. Ian clears Demo done in 42 days and loses 85% of his deals, which reads as velocity without qualification. Ben believes the underlying demo problems are now fixed.
entries.metric: Ian Hill's new-business win rate, and his Demo done cycle time
entries.target: First review point, not a target
entries.note: One month of closed outcomes is a small sample. Read it as direction, not proof.
